title: The old harper
hookLine: an old musician, abandoned by his audience, plays for God alone in a graveyard (Masnavi 1.1913ff)

lines: APPLAUSE IS A KIND OF FOOD.
cards: The wedding singer everybody once wanted. The athlete twenty years after the last game. Anyone who was once very good at something, and then the calls stopped.
Applause is a kind of food, and when it goes, the hunger can be hard to admit. Rumi tells a story about what someone does when the crowd has gone home for good.
It's the first of three days with one character: the old harper.

teach.h: A SINGER WHO MADE NIGHTINGALES FAINT.
teach.b: It's in Book One of the Masnavi, Rumi's long poem of stories. In the days of Umar, the second caliph after the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, a harper lived in Medina.
Rumi says his voice made nightingales lose their senses, and one breath of his song could make a gathering feel alive. Then he grew old.
His voice cracked. His hands got stiff. The voice that once charmed hearts was now so harsh that nobody wanted it.
The invitations stopped. He had no money, and nothing else he knew how to do. So one day he took his harp out of the city to the graveyard.
And there, among the graves, where no one could hear, he played. Rumi has him say something like this: all my life you gave me breath, and I spent it on others.

Now I'll play for you, God, and you'll have to be my patron, because no one else will pay. He played and wept until he fell asleep with his head on a grave, the harp as his pillow. Notice what's happened.
He's playing badly, alone, for an audience he can't see. For the first time in his life, the playing isn't for applause. The song has nowhere to go but upward.

Some readers hear themselves in him: everything people do for someone to notice, and the strange freedom of doing one thing for no one at all. What happens next is tomorrow. Your line: play for no one.

how: Readers of the Masnavi often read its stories slowly, a section at a time, and in Sufi circles this story is told as a picture of doing good work for God alone, not for praise.

games.q: you're the harper. your voice is gone, the invitations have stopped, and you have no money. what do you do?
o: keep knocking on doors, hoping for one more wedding.
take your harp to the graveyard and play for God alone.
sell the harp and never play again.
games.why: he walks out to the graveyard and plays among the graves, for God, until he falls asleep on his harp.

practice: Sit for a moment where nobody is watching, nobody is scoring, and nothing will be posted. Breathe, and notice if part of you still wants to do this well for someone. Let that part rest.

wordCard.voice: Umar, the second caliph after the Prophet Muhammad, who in Rumi's story is sent by a dream to a graveyard. Today's word.

orig.note: Persian: the harp, the old musician's instrument in Rumi's story. the Persian story is called the tale of the old harper.

carryVoice: Your line: play for no one. The harper is still asleep on his harp. See you tomorrow.
